notes: Identity assessed independently from the supplied text: title page names The impact of Screen Time, Social Media Use and Extraversion on Life Satisfaction among University Students: An extended replication study; Sara von Pruski; Department of Psychology, University of Twente; Bachelor Thesis; date 01.07.2024. Supplied source URL identifies essay.utwente.nl file/100459, agreeing with the neutral reference identifier. This is the primary thesis report, with results, discussion, references and appendices through PDF page 78, rather than an abstract-only parse or preregistration. No DOI is printed for this thesis. No source PDF path was supplied, so PDF layout was not independently rendered. Target remains ambiguous: p.27 describes the extended parallel mediation and refers forward to Table 3 on p.28. The neutral description says time spent using social media but does not distinguish total screen time (which includes non-social-media activities), passive social media use, or active social media use. Table 3 prints the extraversion paths: TST B=-0.41, SE=0.12, t=-3.38, p=.001* (narrative p.27 gives p<.05); PSMU B=0.28, SE=0.19, t=1.51, p=.14; ASMU B=-0.12, SE=0.21, t=-0.59, p=.56. These are candidate printed B coefficients; no conversion or standardisation inference made. Table 2 also gives bivariate r candidates EX/TST=-.29**, EX/PSMU=.16 and EX/ASMU=-.04. These are distinct tests and are not merged with the regression coefficients. Authors describe the TST direction as opposite to Bunz but the passive/active paths as inconsistent with other literature; no unique target-specific replication verdict is established. Analytic N unresolved: p.20 reports 149 recruited, not a critical-model analytic N. P.24 retains incomplete cases in the dataset; p.35 states missing values were automatically removed from analyses. P.35 refers to sample size 92 in the multiple regression discussion and 94 for the moderation interaction, while p.36 describes current samples varying between 91 and 94. These are candidate author-labelled sample counts only; exact target correspondence and the mediation sample are not independently established. No N inferred from df, recruitment count, code execution, or arithmetic. Only assigned unfinished fields were assessed. Unassigned original and p fields are placeholders.
